lesson.title: Case clinic: a learning and employment platform
lesson.summary: Separate platform functions and trace changed decisions across learning and work.

prerequisites.reason: The platform case contrasts identity confirmation with identity discovery.
The platform case includes evaluation of learning outcomes.
The platform case includes candidate filtering. The platform case includes task allocation based on individual behaviour.

blocks: **Platform-function assessment** checks each concrete intended use within a platform. Northbridge's fictional platform offers document conversion, programme admission recommendations, applicant ranking and exam-behaviour detection.
A general 'learning and work assistant' title does not select one legal category for all functions. Map users, inputs, outputs, affected people and decisions for each.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 1–4; Articles 3(12), 5, 6

blocks: Admission recommendations need comparison with educational access; candidate ranking needs recruitment comparison; exam monitoring needs its own educational point. These are separate purposes even if one model powers all of them.

Document conversion has different facts. It does not prove that the platform's other functions are equally narrow. Assess whether each function is part of the same system or a genuinely separate system boundary.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 1–4; Articles 3(12), 5, 6

blocks: Changed fact: a supposedly neutral conversion tool extracts personal features and assigns applicant scores before the recruiter sees them. The assessment must use that actual evaluative function.
A component's internal name does not eliminate its contribution to decisions. Identify profiling and material influence questions, and collect evidence rather than asserting a derogation.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 1–4; Articles 3(12), 5, 6

blocks: The case clinic ends with a record of each function's relevant point and open tests. Check prohibitions before permission is assumed, then paragraph 3, scope, dates and other law.
An unresolved boundary or feature should be explicit. A platform-wide 'safe' conclusion based on its least consequential feature is not supported by the case facts.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 1–4; Articles 3(12), 5, 6
